goal: A 30-second birthday film from the 12 phone clips and the song: the year in twelve beats, cut to the music, ending on the people.
audience: the person whose birthday it is (and everyone at the party)
assumptions: the song is the clock: cuts on its beats
the 12 clips are the human's own files (their license is their attestation)
the footage is the 12 named phone clips (the count is twelve — the plan takes all twelve)
the named song is the music bed (the one track the human chose)
the bed is mixed, not pasted: it lands at the loudness target as one mix
no format was named: the plan states its assumption (16:9, landscape phone clips)
the 12 phone clips are missing: flagged in feasibility; the song too: flagged in feasibility

decision.why: A montage of real clips cut to a real song: the edit technique measures the song (its beats land the cuts — the montage preset), ingests the clips once, and the music bed rule ducks nothing here because the song IS the piece.

alternatives.rejected_because: the clips are the content — a designed piece without them would not be a birthday film

alternatives.id: simplest: the 12 clips in order, 2.5 seconds each
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — and the arithmetic is right — but 12 equal beats ignores the song's shape; the chorus deserves the best clip

segments.brief: Ingest the 12 clips and the song; measure the song's beats; cut each clip to its moment (the best frames, not the first); end on the people. Captions: names if the human gives them.
acceptance: every cut within 1 frame of a beat
the last beat is the payoff
it reads as a birthday video: a celebratory arc, the people at the end
the montage is paced to the song: cuts land on its measured beats
the montage uses the twelve clips: no clip twice, the best frames of each
the bed is mixed, not pasted: ducked 10-14 dB under any clip speech

assembly.transitions: cuts on the beat (a birthday montage does not crossfade)

blocked_inputs: the 12 phone clips do not exist (the human must supply them)
the song does not exist (the human must supply it)

risks: mixed phone formats (portrait + landscape) — the design picks one orientation and letterboxes honestly
